statement: Two general complex circles have four distinct common affine tangent lines.
notes:
The n>=3 formula 3*2^(n-1) does not apply at n=2. Equivalently, intersect the two dual conics and use Bezout; generic intersections are ordinary affine tangent lines.

This n=2 assertion is an elementary classical two-circle calculation, included here as a deduction; it is not attributed as a new theorem of Sottile–Theobald, whose general-dimensional theorem assumes n≥3.
